preflight.initialReason: Issue #12 first measurement: the merge base has no local check workload. After an untimed warm-up build on both sides, time the typecheck, lint, unit and parity lanes once and measure native peak RSS. The five-minute ceiling comes from issue #12 and covers the checks with their builds; elapsed time and memory are compared with the warm merge base using a 50% margin.

harness.initialReason: Issue #48 first measurement: the merge base has no harness. The lane runs only when a change touches the harness, its hook or its launch facts, since each run spends plan usage. It runs every scripted session once, on real agents, and holds each to 60 s and all of them to 10 minutes on the reference Mac. Model latency moves a single run far more than a code change does, so a later merge base's runs are compared with a 100% margin.

tasks.initialReason: Issue #12 first measurement: the merge base has no executable benchmark. Measure skeleton process startup, not issue #17 hook overhead, in 20 rounds interleaved with the merge base. p50 and peak memory get a 50% relative margin and the design's 10 MB peak-memory ceiling; p95 is reported, since its tail moves past that margin between identical binaries. Established definitions are frozen.

Issue #246 first measurement: the merge base has no repo-rules check. Time the lint lane's rules on this repo in 20 rounds: one read of every file git lists, one cargo metadata call and the size diff against the merge base. Issue #246 caps p50 at 1 s, p95 at 2 s and peak memory at 128 MB; later merge bases hold p50 and peak memory to a 50% margin.

Issue #15 first measurement: the merge base has no evidence store. One process runs one put of a 5 MB PNG screenshot against a temp store, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-call limits stay in tests/acceptance/15/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #15 first measurement: the merge base has no evidence store. One process runs one text put of 8 MB of output, scrubbed by pattern and by 16 held values against a temp store, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-call limits stay in tests/acceptance/15/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #15 first measurement: the merge base has no evidence store. One process runs one retention pass over 36 days of records at 500 a day against a temp store, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-call limits stay in tests/acceptance/15/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #56 first measurement: the merge base has no hub core. The bench starts the plain TypeScript spike hub, holds one hook in each of 50 sessions on a check that passes at once, and prints hold latency, the hub's peak memory and its leaked handles; perf times the whole bench in 20 rounds and caps its peak memory at 250 MB, about twice what the hub and its bench use together. p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against a later merge base, since a run that starts processes moves with machine load.

Issue #56 first measurement: the merge base has no hub core. The bench starts the Effect 4 spike hub, holds one hook in each of 50 sessions on a check that passes at once, and prints hold latency, the hub's peak memory and its leaked handles; perf times the whole bench in 20 rounds and caps its peak memory at 250 MB, about twice what the hub and its bench use together. p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against a later merge base, since a run that starts processes moves with machine load.

Issue #311 first measurement: a new task, with nothing to compare against: before this change there are no event kinds for it to validate. One process validates the first fixture of each of the 59 event kinds 1,000 times, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-event limit (20 µs at p95 on the reference Mac) stays in tests/acceptance/311/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #47 first measurement: the merge base has no fixture corpus. One process replays every recorded payload under adapters/corpus through its adapter and compares it with its stored events, field by field. Issue #47 caps the full replay at 2 minutes on the reference Mac; later merge bases hold p50 and peak memory to a 50% margin.

Issue #14 first measurement: the merge base has no record package. One process opens a record in a temp folder and appends 20,000 stream events fired 200 at a time, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-call limits (5,000 events a second, 2 ms p95) stay in tests/acceptance/14/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #14 first measurement: the merge base has no record package. One process appends a 100,000-event log, then drops every projection and rebuilds it by replay, so p50 includes the appends and Node's start and the replay's own limits (60 s per million events, 100 MB of working memory) stay in tests/acceptance/14/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #319 first measurement: the merge base has the asks core (#318) but no task for it. One process drafts ask settings into a temp home, opens a record and the asks core, and raises and answers 200 asks one after another, so p50 includes Node's start and the per-call limit (under 5 ms to create or answer) stays in tests/acceptance/319/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #319 first measurement: the merge base has the asks core (#318) but no task for it. One process appends 10,000 open asks over 2,000 sessions and loads the inbox projection once, so p50 includes the appends and Node's start and the load's own limit (under 100 ms) stays in tests/acceptance/319/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.

Issue #42 first measurement: the merge base has no OTLP receiver. One process starts the receiver on a temp record and sends it 20,000 Claude Code spans as 100 protobuf trace exports of 200, the AC6 load without its pacing, so p50 includes Node's start and the sustained limits (2,000 spans a second under 5% of a core and 50 MB) stay in tests/acceptance/42/budgets.test.ts; p50 and peak memory get a 50% margin against the merge base once main has this task.
